title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies automorphisms u = u_ξ = u_{ξ,η} = u_{α,β} of the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3}, the free profinite group on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. These are elements of a group M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0), which he identifies with N_{0,3}^{!≈}, and they lie in the circle of ideas around the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Each u has a 'multiplicator' μ ∈ Ẑ^* (the analogue of λ in GT) with μ = 2ν+1, where ν plays the role of m = (λ−1)/2 in Drinfeld's relations. His 'fundamental relations' (14), (15) are the analogues of the 3-cycle and 2-cycle (hexagon-type) relations. In them, ρ is the order-3 rotation of {0,1,∞}, σ_∞ (and τ_∞) are order-2 symmetries, and φ̂ is the automorphism attached to u.

Previous page: he introduced auxiliary parameters α, β with ζ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}. Assuming α_3 = 0, he derived (56): ζ is a ρ-coboundary of the element φ̂(ρ^{-1}(β^{-1})).

This page draws the conclusion. In the case μ ≡ 1 mod 3 (equivalently ν ≡ 0 mod 3, i.e. the mod-3 character E_3(μ) = 1), the pair of relations (14)+(15) is equivalent to either one of two relations:
- (57) ξ = φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})) · ρ(φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})))^{-1}. This exhibits ξ as an explicit coboundary x ρ(x)^{-1} for the Z/3-action given by ρ.
- (58) ξ = φ̂(η) · σ_∞(φ̂(η))^{-1} · l_1^ν, with ν ∈ Ẑ and ν ≡ 0 mod 3. This is a Z/2-coboundary twisted by a power of l_1.
These relations characterize the elements u_ξ whose multiplicator is ≡ 1 mod 3. The margin stresses that the reformulation is valid only under μ ≡ 1 mod 3. In modern terms: the cocycle conditions (ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 and the 2-cycle condition) become explicit coboundary representations. The obstruction to doing this uniformly depends on λ mod 3, i.e. it is cohomology of Z/3.

Remark: apart from the identity, the only element of M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0) that can be computed by explicit solution is τ ∈ T_{0,3}^! ⊂ N_{0,3}^{!≈}, corresponding to τ_∞. Its invariants are listed in (59): h = β_0 = 1, f = 1, α = α_0 = τ_∞, ξ = g = l_1^{-1}, η = 1, ν = −1, μ = −1. This is the 'complex conjugation' element (λ, f) = (−1, 1) of GT.
- He checks the 3-cycle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1, which here reduces to l_0^{-1}l_1^{-1}l_∞^{-1} = 1, i.e. it follows from l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1 in a suitable order.
- He notes that here α_3 = 1. Since μ = −1 ≢ 1 mod 3, the new relation (57) does not apply; one must use (54) with i = 1, α_3 = 1, as stated at the top of p. 426.
- An attempted verification of (54) for this element is crossed out.

Next page: he shows that η = 1 forces ξ = l_1^ν. An SL(2,Ẑ) argument then gives ν ∈ {0, −1}, i.e. only the identity and τ_∞.
errors: The transcription of (57) has η^{-1} inside the second factor. By analogy with (56) on the previous page, and judging from the image, both factors should be evaluated at the same argument ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}), so that (57) is a coboundary xρ(x)^{-1}. This is a transcription issue, not a mathematical one.
The order-2 automorphism in (58) is read as τ_∞, but the parametrization η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} on p. 424–425 suggests σ_∞. The symbol is ambiguous in the image.

The check of ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 for ξ = l_1^{-1} silently depends on the convention for how ρ permutes l_0, l_1, l_∞ and on the order of the product. It is correct up to these conventions. No genuine mathematical error is visible, and the crossed-out lines show Grothendieck abandoning one verification route.

ideas.what: In the case μ ≡ 1 mod 3, the two fundamental (3-cycle and 2-cycle) relations are equivalent to a single explicit coboundary representation of ξ: either as xρ(x)^{-1} (Z/3) or as yσ(y)^{-1}·l_1^ν (Z/2).
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological (coboundary) interpretation of the hexagon / 2-cycle relations of GT; vanishing of H^1 of Z/2, Z/3 acting on the profinite free group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990; 2-cycle solutions written as g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y)); Lochak–Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (1997)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme or La Longue Marche as far as known; only in these unpublished notes.

ideas.what: The mod-3 condition on the multiplicator, μ ≡ 1 (3), i.e. E_3(μ) = 1, as the condition under which the reformulation holds.
ideas.modern_name: Mod-3 character of λ ∈ Ẑ^* governing the 3-cycle relation (via m = (λ−1)/2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related remarks appear in GT literature (Ihara, Lochak–Schneps)

ideas.what: The explicit element τ_∞ with μ = −1, f = 1, ξ = l_1^{-1}, as the only nontrivial element computable explicitly.

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently arrives at a cohomological (coboundary) reformulation of the GT-type relations, valid when the multiplicator μ ≡ 1 mod 3. This anticipates in spirit the Lochak–Schneps cohomological interpretation of GT, with the mod-3 restriction made explicit.
missed.quote: valable seulement si ν≡0 (3) i.e. μ≡1 (3) i.e. E_3(μ)=1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical priority. The explicit splitting by μ mod 3, and the formulation via automorphisms φ̂ rather than via f, might give a slightly different parametrization of the subgroup of \hat{GT} (or of Grothendieck's variant) with λ ≡ 1 mod 3. This is worth comparing with Lochak–Schneps, but is probably not new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an intermediate computation in the systematic study of the 'équation des lacets'. The coboundary reformulation is close to known results (Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps), and the explicit element is just complex conjugation. The mod-3 condition is a nice detail but not likely to surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'équivalent ensemble à l'une des deux relations' ('relations' is written in the margin along the arrow).
(57): the second factor is probably ρ(φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})))^{-1}, same argument as the first factor, not η^{-1}.
(58): the involution is possibly σ_∞ rather than τ_∞.
Margin: 'valable seulement si ν≡0 (3) i.e. μ≡1 (3) i.e. E_3(μ)=1'.

Remark: 'Le seul élément de M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0) ≃ N_{0,3}^{!≈} qui se calcule par solutions explicites, en dehors de l'élément unité (et l'unique des N_{0,3}^{!∼} ⊃ N_{0,3}^{!≈}) est l'élément τ ∈ T_{0,3}^! ⊂ N_{0,3}^{!≈} qui correspond à l'élément τ_∞ ... = u_ξ = u_{ξ,η}, pour'. The 'ne' insertion is doubtful.
Bottom-left margin: 'Attention, ici α_3=1 donc (57) valable [?] ...'.
Bottom: 'où ξ, ν satisfont bien à ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 i.e. l_0^{-1}l_1^{-1}l_∞^{-1}=1, et aux relations (54) pour ...'. The rest is crossed out.
